children: The recent U.S. exit of Australia's Guzman y Gomez raises doubts at Jefferies about the portability of the concept. Initiating coverage of the Mexican-themed fast-food franchiser with a hold rating, Jefferies analysts see Guzman y Gomez's decision to quit the U.S. after sales failed to meet management expectations as a significant setback. They acknowledge that management still believe the brand can have global appeal, but tell clients in a note they have doubts about its viability at scale outside Australia. Valuation looks full on current projections, but the company has a solid track record of like-for-like sales growth, they add. Jefferies puts a target price of 27.00 Australian dollars on the stock. Shares are down 2.1% at A$25.06. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
